title: Partial save API must read-modify-write against stored state, not merge with defaults
trigger: A save API accepts Partial<T> and implicitly promises to merge with current state, but the implementation merges with DEFAULT instead
principle: An API accepting Partial<T> implicitly promises to merge with the current stored state. If the implementation merges with DEFAULT instead, any field absent from the partial resets to default — a partial save wipes every other field. Partial save must read-modify-write: load current → merge partial → write. DEFAULT is only a fallback for fields missing from stored state, not the base for every save. Callers passing full settings are unaffected (full merged with full = full, idempotent). Watch for recursion: if save calls load and load has a persist-back migration that calls save, break the cycle by having the migration write directly to storage.

cases.context: saveSettings(partial) merges with DEFAULT_SETTINGS instead of stored settings → a caller passing only {navClusterPosition} wipes buttonSize/bgOpacity/buttonOpacity back to defaults; another passing only {subtitleOffset} wipes ALL other fields
After making saveSettings call loadSettings, the loadSettings persist-back migration (which called saveSettings) becomes infinite recursion: load → migrate → save → load → migrate → ...

applyFor: Settings / KV stores with a save(Partial<T>) API — must read-modify-write, not merge with defaults
Any partial update API that implicitly promises a merge (Redux dispatch partial, Zustand partial set)
Migration persist-back paths — avoid recursion when save calls load (have migration write directly to storage)
Designing a Partial<T> API — be explicit: merge with current state (read-modify-write) vs replace (caller must pass full)
